title: Environment watch
summary: The pair to LLM data: it finds what needs fixing - skill files that never reach the model, mapped paths that do not resolve, error lines in the background - and stays green only when nothing does.

surfaces.usb: N/A(not promoted yet - the steward scoped this module to the PC edition first; its pane slot is 'dock', the bottom strip, which so far is a PC-only shell change, so the module and the strip must be promoted together)
surfaces.web: DEGRADED(a browser tab has no disk, no engine and no log files: on the web this card renders and reports that its checks could not run rather than claiming the environment is good)

notes: Read-only finder, the pair to lygo.llminfo: that module answers 'what is hooked up', this one answers 'what needs fixing'. It owns no state, writes nothing, gates nothing and fixes nothing - a watcher that also repaired would hide the thing it found, so its gate is 'none' and the tests scan its own source for write calls. Three rules shape it: a finding is a fact with a LOCATION (a path, a file, a log line), a search that did not run is reported UNCHECKED by name and holds the card out of green, and the search is STATED - the panel prints its narrow log rule table and how many checks ran, so 'nothing needs fixing' is a claim about a named search and never a vibe. Its family suffix is 'watch' (a finder: amber or red when something needs fixing) against lygo.llminfo's 'info' (a read-out), per 01_DESIGN/MODULE_NAMING_AND_BRANDING_v1.md. The pane id is slot-prefixed ('dock.env') because /api/modules publishes pane ids and the shell places a pane by its prefix; slot 'dock' is the bottom strip, full length, one card per module, with the page scrolling to it, and inner_scroll is false on purpose.
